Article (2) of the regulation bars a bank from acting as a payment token issuer itself (it may set up a licensed subsidiary, affiliate or related entity to do so) and limits a licensed issuer to issuing Dirham Payment Tokens to UAE residents. Zand Trust's transparency page lists both deployments with 6 decimals. Onboarded institutions mint and redeem through Zand Bank's corporate platform, and the issuer says AEDZ is also available on partner exchanges. Exactly 1,000,000,000 AEDZ of that sits in eleven wallets, five on Ethereum and six on Solana, that each received a single transfer on September 30 or October 7 2026 and have not moved it. The issuer counts these balances as circulating: its October 1 2026 attestation matched the full on-chain supply, and its daily feed showed 1.01 billion AEDZ on October 30 2026. The wallets that receive every mint hold about 2 million AEDZ. CoinGecko's zand-aed is a preview listing with no price, market cap or tickers, DefiLlama does not track AEDZ, and no DEX pool exists.

coins.name: BILS
coins.launchPhaseDetail: Bits of Gold, a Tel Aviv-based licensed crypto broker/custodian operating since 2013, received full regulatory approval on April 28 2026 from Israel's Capital Market, Insurance and Savings Authority (CMISA) to issue BILS, the first regulated shekel-pegged stablecoin, following a two-year sandbox pilot approved in March 2024. Backed 1:1 by New Israeli Shekels held in segregated dedicated bank accounts within Israel (foreign custody excluded), audited by Ernst & Young, with Fireblocks custody/issuance infrastructure and QEDIT zero-knowledge privacy, issued on Solana via token extensions. The regulator mandates a deliberately gradual, small-scale rollout (likely institutional/qualified participants first) before wide availability; no firm public-launch date set. On November 1 2026 the Solana mint (CDxFUPSRK4dC68jWV7SCPezU1vNYXz87Y6fjhhRvsuhd) still held 100,000 BILS, unchanged since August 6 2026, although 268 transactions touched the mint between October 23 and October 29 2026. A further 100,000 BILS were minted on November 15 2026, the first supply change since August, taking the Solana supply to 200,000 BILS. On November 1 the bils.co.il transparency page showed 100K ILS of BILS in circulation, matching the supply at that time, and 105K ILS in total reserves; its 1.1M figure is a fixed total-supply label on the Solana and Ethereum tabs that neither contract supports. The Ethereum address the site lists, 0x24B3785B4Ec3eBB20Af43Cc3A132D86e0b936171, is a test token named 'Test BILS ETH', so Pharos records no Ethereum deployment. On August 16 2026 Bits of Gold disclosed a breach of up to 250,000 customers' personal details through a third-party analytics provider, reporting it to CMISA with funds unaffected. The transparency page lists the EY Q3 2026 report as pending, and the white paper served as new in September 2026 is internally dated June 2025. CoinGecko carries the mint with no price or tickers. Distinct from Israel's broader Stablecoin Law, which remains in draft/public-comment stage. Pharos tracks the ILS peg as OTHER until shekel peg support is built.
